paper_summary: Hungarian conference paper (Muszaki Tudomanyos Kozlemenyek 13, 2020) on bimodal A413 cast-aluminium matrix syntactic foams filled with high-purity Al2O3 ceramic hollow spheres of two nominal diameters (d1 = 2.4 mm and d2 = 7.0 mm) mixed in equal volume ratio and infiltrated by low-pressure (300 kPa Ar) infiltration (spheres preheated 500 C / 45 min, melt at 650 C, 5 s infiltration). The foams reached 1.61+/-0.03 g/cm3 against a theoretical 1.4 g/cm3 (A413 matrix is 2.66 g/cm3); CT scans revealed aluminium leaking into some spheres and shrinkage-induced inclusions in the matrix. Quasi-static compression (5 mm/min, evaluated to ISO 13314:2011) gave 120+/-29 MPa compressive strength at 5.39 % strain, a 77+/-18 MPa plateau stress, 43.50+/-16.82 J/cm3 absorbed energy and 64.22 % energy-absorption efficiency, with the matrix separating from the spheres during collapse.

records.sample_label: Bimodal A413 / Al2O3 ceramic hollow sphere syntactic foam (d1 = 2.4 mm : d2 = 7.0 mm, 1:1 by volume)

processing.matrix_name: A413 casting aluminium alloy (11.0-13.0 wt% Si, max 1.3 Fe, 1.0 Cu, max 0.5 Ni, 0.35 Mn, max 0.15 Sn, 0.1 Mg, balance Al)
processing.particle_grade: High-purity Al2O3 ceramic hollow spheres, bimodal: nominal d1 = 2.4 mm and d2 = 7.0 mm mixed in equal volume ratio (1:1)

structure.microstructure_notes: Measured density 1.61 +/- 0.03 g/cm3 (the conclusions round it to 1.62 g/cm3) versus 2.66 g/cm3 for the bulk A413 matrix. The theoretical packing fraction of the 1:1 bimodal sphere mixture is 72.8 % from the Brouwers analytical model (against ~64 % for random close packing of a single size), which would give a theoretical foam density of 1.4 g/cm3; the measured density is higher because the sphere diameters are not two discrete values and their circularity carries a 6-8 % average error. CT scans show aluminium that leaked into some hollow spheres (raising density), a few defective spheres, and shrinkage-induced inclusions (unwanted porosity) in the matrix that were not quantified. During compression the foams disintegrated and the matrix-to-sphere bond was lost.

test.specimen_notes: Quasi-static upsetting (compression) test on an Instron 5989 universal electromechanical machine with a 600 kN load cell, crosshead speed 5 mm/min; results evaluated per ISO 13314:2011. Specimen dimensions and number of repeats are not stated (the paper reports mean +/- standard deviation and notes large scatter due to the randomness of the packing).

The produced metal foams have a density of 1.61±0.03 g/cm3, with smaller inclusions and some defective hollow spheres in the structure. The foams have an average compressive strength of 120 MPa and a specific mechanical energy absorbing capacity of 43.5 J/cm3.
Two hollow spheres of different nominal diameters (d1 = 2.4 mm and d2 = 7.0 mm) were used in equal volume ratio.

extraction_notes: Four-page Hungarian/English conference paper read in full including the [TABLE] blocks. Only one material (one bimodal composition) and one test condition (quasi-static compression) are reported, hence a single record. Mapping and conversions from Table 2 (ISO 13314:2011 notation): sigma_c = 120 +/- 29 MPa (maximum stress / compressive strength) -> strength_mpa; eps_c = 5.39 +/- 0.80 % (strain at maximum stress) -> strain_at_failure = 0.0539; sigma_pl = 77 +/- 18 MPa -> plateau_stress_mpa; eps_ple = 54.31 +/- 0.86 % (plateau end strain, i.e. onset of densification per ISO 13314) -> densification_strain = 0.5431; W = 43.50 +/- 16.82 J/cm3 -> energy_absorption_mj_m3 = 43.5 (1 J/cm3 = 1 MJ/m3). Values not representable in the schema: W_c = 3.23 +/- 1.33 J/cm3 (energy absorbed up to the compressive strength point) and W_e = 64.22 +/- 0.96 % (energy absorption efficiency); the standard deviations of all quantities also have no schema field. No elastic modulus is reported. particle_volume_fraction was left null on purpose: the paper gives only a THEORETICAL packing fraction of 72.8 % from the Brouwers analytical model for a 1:1 bimodal sphere mixture and explicitly states that this calculated value is in error for the real material (measured density 1.61 g/cm3 vs the 1.4 g/cm3 predicted from that packing); no measured filler fraction is given. particle_mean_diameter_um was left null because the filler is bimodal with two nominal diameters (2400 um and 7000 um) mixed 1:1 by volume, so no single mean diameter is stated; the two sizes are recorded in particle_grade. Sphere wall thickness and true density are not given (referred to an earlier paper, ref. [13]). cure_or_process_temperature_c = 650 C is the matrix melt temperature (T_matrix) from Table 1; the other infiltration parameters (sphere preheat 500 C for 45 min, infiltration pressure 300 kPa Ar for 5 s) have no schema field and are recorded here. Test temperature is not stated (room temperature implied) and the strain rate is not given - only a 5 mm/min crosshead speed with no specimen height - so both are null. Figures 2-4 (CT slice, scatter band of the compression curves, failed specimens) contain no readable numerical values. Hungarian evidence quotes are transliterated to ASCII (accents removed) but are otherwise verbatim; the English abstract quote is exactly verbatim.
